summary: Building an AdminPanel with backend-backed Question Gallery management; Day 2 backend/API checks completed and proceeding to Day 3 to implement full Question Gallery CRUD and persistence.
architectural_notes: Day 3 scope includes Question Gallery CRUD APIs and frontend wiring in AdminPanel.
Ensure gallery questions are stored in stable/persistent storage to survive upgrades.
If questions include images, implement image upload/storage handling end-to-end.

existing_features.title: Wire the AdminPanel Question Gallery UI to the real backend Question Gallery APIs by updating React Query hooks and components so that selecting a subject loads questions from the backend instead of returning an empty stub.

Add Admin UI support for creating and editing gallery questions (including optional images) within the existing AdminPanel QuestionManagementPanel flow, and connect it to the new backend create/update APIs.

new_feature_requests.summary: Day 3: Implement Question Gallery backend APIs (add/get/delete/update) and connect AdminPanel UI to make upload/display/delete/edit functional
Day 3: Add persistent stable storage so gallery questions persist across upgrades/redeploys
Day 3: Support storing/handling image uploads for gallery questions (if used by UI)

Implement backend (Motoko) Question Gallery APIs to support full CRUD for questions, including: create a new question, list questions filtered by subject, update an existing question, and delete a question. Enforce admin-only access for create/update/delete and allow authenticated users to read/list questions.
Add persistent stable storage for Question Gallery data so questions (and associated counters/indices needed for listing and CRUD) survive canister upgrades/redeploys.

Support storing and returning question images for gallery questions using the existing blob-storage mixin (Storage.ExternalBlob fields already present in Question/Option types). Provide backend methods needed by the frontend to attach uploaded images to a question (question-level image and option-level image).
